Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow-up this week if that helps move things faster.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for sending the SOC 2 summary. That’s helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

1) Pen test: For our security review, we typically accept a redacted executive summary (vendor identity redacted) plus a confirmation that the test was performed by a qualified 3rd party within the last 12 months. If we need to escalate, procurement may request an unredacted copy under our standard NDA.
2) Vulnerability management: we need the following details at minimum:
   - Scanning cadence (SAST/DAST and external vulnerability scans)
   - SLA for critical/important findings (time-to-remediate expectations)
   - Disclosure policy (how you notify customers of findings that affect them)

If Stephanie can share those bullets in an email, that will probably be sufficient for our initial review. If anything is borderline, we may ask for a short call with your security team.

Please CC our procurement contact if you share any agreements.

Thanks,
Claire
Senior Information Security Manager | FinHealth
claire.zhang@finhealth.com

Note: procurement contact is Alex Gomez (cc’d).

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pen test & vuln management follow-up (FinHealth)

Hi all —

Adding the Redwood secops summary and answers to the items Claire listed. Short version below; happy to expand or hop on a call.

- Pen test status: External pentest completed 2026-11-15 by GreyShield Security (3rd party). We can provide a redacted executive summary showing findings and remediation status. Full report is available under NDA.
- Scanning cadence:
  * SAST: weekly automated runs against our CI with critical alerts triaged immediately.
  * DAST: monthly internal scans for staging endpoints; quarterly external scans against production-facing endpoints.
  * External vuln scans (authenticated + unauthenticated): weekly for high-sensitivity production clusters, monthly for others.
- Vulnerability SLAs (time-to-remediate target):
  * Critical (CVSS >= 9.0): 72 hours to mitigation plan, 14 days to remediation where feasible.
  * High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): 7 days to mitigation plan, 30 days for remediation.
  * Medium/Low: triaged per sprint, remediation window varies.
- Disclosure policy: Customers are notified via in-product status and email within 24 hours for critical vulnerabilities that materially affect data confidentiality or availability. We also publish post-incident summaries to validated contacts.
- Proof/Artifacts: we can provide the redacted pen-test executive summary, the SOC 2 summary (attached), and our vulnerability management policy excerpt. For procurement, we typically provide an artifacts bundle via secure link or under NDA.

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf (PDF), PenTest-exec-summary-redacted.pdf (PDF, redacted)

Marissa — if Claire confirms they want the redacted summary now, I’ll prepare the bundle and share via a protected link. Rishi — tagging you for any legal redlines or if procurement will need a contract addendum for sharing the full report.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
